input: A gravity settler is used to remove calcium carbonate from a process stream, and it is sized on the basis of an overflow rate of 0.92 m h-1. At a throughput of 308 m3 h-1, this rate requires a plan area of 335 m2. The overflow rate can be understood as the throughput divided by the plan area, and it is the controlling figure for the settler: a particle that settles faster than the overflow rate will reach the bottom of the vessel before the flow carries it out, whereas a particle that settles more slowly will leave together with the clarified stream. The plan area of 335 m2 is therefore determined by the rate at which the process stream is allowed to rise through the vessel, rather than by the depth of the vessel, and at the stated throughput the area follows directly from the rate of 0.92 m h-1. Calcium carbonate is the solid that the basis names, and the design overflow rate is a vendor rule for this solid: it is the vendor's figure for the rate at which this material can be loaded, and it is drawn from the vendor's practice rather than from a test on the stream that is to be treated. It is important to note that no settling test on the actual slurry has been carried out. The size of the settler thus rests on a rule whose value for the actual slurry, with its own particle sizes and concentrations, remains unverified; a settling test would either confirm the rate of 0.92 m h-1 and the area of 335 m2 that it produces at 308 m3 h-1, or replace both of them with figures that have been measured on the material itself.
